LIU Eric James (26039986g)

ZHU Kecheng (26118866g)
SCRIPT 01  •  English and Chinese preparation notes

Hello, we are Safari. Our project examines walking navigation among newcomers to Hong Kong. We want to understand what information people need, how they handle it while responding to their surroundings, and when it helps or adds interaction burden. Today, we will explain the literature behind our focus, our planned fieldwork and analysis, and the decisions still to be resolved. Our intended outcome is a contextual information classification with preliminary design guidance.
我们研究初到香港者如何处理步行导航信息。今天讲研究依据、实地流程、分析方法及待确定事项。目标是初步的信息分类与设计建议，不是已经做好的产品或已经验证的安全方案。
Sources and material notes  •  not part of the spoken script
Word v2: Slides 1–2. Cover photo: Unsplash YheOCC-64hg; urban context only, not our selected route or fieldwork.
Proposed timing: confirm in the independent pilot
Explain Google Maps and the procedure
Participant-paced navigation; log T0 and end
Open account, 3–5 episodes and closing checks
Two researchers: observation / safety and recording
Walk at the participant’s pace. No questions at crossings or stairs.
60 minutes is a pilot target, not a measured guarantee
SCRIPT 07  •  English and Chinese preparation notes

Our proposed session has four stages: ten minutes for consent, background and device checks; five minutes for unrelated practice; around twenty minutes for the main walk; and twenty-five minutes for debrief, episode review and closing. This sixty-minute budget is a pilot target, not a measured guarantee. Two researchers will cover observation and safety, and recording. We will mark the formal start and end and document any interventions. Participants should walk at their own pace. We will not hurry them or ask questions at crossings and stairs, and safety takes priority over uninterrupted recording.
拟定 10 分钟准备、5 分钟练习、20 分钟步行、25 分钟回顾，共约 60 分钟，要经过 pilot 测试。两人负责观察／安全与录制，记录起止和干预。不给速度目标，不在危险位置提问。
Sources and material notes  •  not part of the spoken script
Word v2 Slide 7 and Appendices B–D. These durations are project proposals, not course-prescribed times or recorded outcomes.

P2 Slide 02 Research focus and question
P2 Slide 02 Research focus and question
texts.text: How can navigation information be classified by its associated interaction burdens to inform interaction design methods for improving when and how it is presented and delivered?
What does the person need to confirm?
How is information sought and used?
What helps or adds burden in context?

texts.parentName: P2 Slide 02 Research focus and question
texts.text: Expected output: contextual information classes and preliminary timing / delivery guidance
SCRIPT 02  •  English and Chinese preparation notes

Our research question asks how navigation information can be classified by its associated interaction burdens, to inform when and how it is presented and delivered. We will examine information needs, the sequence of visible actions, and participants' explanations of their experience. A phone check may provide useful reassurance, so we will not treat every check as a difficulty. We aim to identify useful support at particular moments.
核心问题是：怎样根据交互负担给导航信息分类，再指导信息的呈现时机与方式。我们一起看信息需要、行为顺序和参与者解释；看手机也可能是在获得帮助，不能直接等同于困难。
Sources and material notes  •  not part of the spoken script
Confirmed Group Research Topic; Word v2 Slide 2 and Appendix E.

texts.parentName: P2 Slide 03 Literature rationale and working gap
P2 Slide 03 Literature rationale and working gap

texts.text: Screen glances relate to stops and errors; causal direction remains unresolved.
Instruction timing varies with people and context.
Tactile delivery has already been studied in everyday use.
Connect information needs, action sequences and reported burdens
How could this connection inform timing and delivery for newcomers on an unfamiliar Hong Kong walk?

texts.parentName: P2 Slide 03 Literature rationale and working gap
texts.text: Provisional focus to investigate; this is not a claim that the field has never been studied
SCRIPT 03  •  English and Chinese preparation notes

The literature gives us useful starting points. Shimokihara and colleagues found associations between screen glances, stops and navigation errors, but could not establish their causal direction. Golab and colleagues studied when pedestrians request instructions, while PocketNavigator explored tactile delivery in everyday use. Our working gap concerns the connection between specific information needs, action sequences and reported burdens for newcomers on an unfamiliar Hong Kong walk. This is a contextual question to investigate. We do not claim that Hong Kong navigation, instruction timing or alternative delivery has never been studied.
已有研究已经讨论屏幕查看、提示时机和触觉导航。我们的切入点是把具体信息需要、行为顺序与报告的帮助／负担连接起来。它是待验证的研究问题，不是“香港导航无人研究”的宣称。
Sources and material notes  •  not part of the spoken script

Shimokihara et al. (2025), doi:10.21037/mhealth-25-33; Golab et al. (2022), doi:10.1080/13875868.2021.1942474; Pielot et al. (2012), doi:10.1145/2207676.2208728. Word v2 Appendix F distinguishes findings, applications and reading limits.

texts.parentName: P2 Slide 04 Paradigm lens and method rationale
P2 Slide 04 Paradigm lens and method rationale

texts.text: Develop useful, contextual and revisable design knowledge.
Multiple Resource Theory (Wickens, 2008) guides questions about possible task interference.
Record visible actions, sequences and the surrounding environment.
Understand what participants sought, what helped and what felt burdensome.
Compare helpful, difficult and ambiguous episodes before proposing information classes.

texts.parentName: P2 Slide 04 Paradigm lens and method rationale
texts.text: Notes, clips and optional GPS do not directly measure cognitive load
SCRIPT 04  •  English and Chinese preparation notes

We adopt pragmatism because we want useful, revisable knowledge about a practical design problem. Our lens focuses on attention allocation and task demands. Multiple Resource Theory helps us consider possible task interference, but does not establish overload from an individual phone check. We plan a focused qualitative field study. Observation documents actions and context; interviews and episode review help explain needs and experience. Notes, clips and optional GPS have different roles. None directly measures cognitive load.
实用主义让我们按实际问题选择方法，形成可修订的设计知识。多重资源理论帮助提出可能解释，不能代替证据。观察看行为，访谈问原因；GPS 只是辅助定位，不是认知负荷测量。
Sources and material notes  •  not part of the spoken script
SD5008 W01 pp.36–38,42; W02 p.36; Wickens (2008), doi:10.1518/001872008X288394; HCI Research Methods Ch.7–8; Word v2 Appendix A.
A separate pilot tests the protocol before the main cases.
Adults who arrived in Hong Kong within six months
Use phone navigation; unfamiliar with the formal route
Voluntary invitations through university or newcomer networks
Peer referrals; retain eligibility when widening channels
Record route familiarity and prior Google Maps experience
Check language; support English or Mandarin
The six-person target is a study plan, not an achieved recruitment count
SCRIPT 05  •  English and Chinese preparation notes

We plan to recruit six adults who arrived in Hong Kong within six months, use phone navigation, and are unfamiliar with the selected route. We will invite volunteers through university or newcomer networks and peer referrals. Screening records route familiarity, language and prior Google Maps experience. Newcomer status and route familiarity are different, so we check both. This exploratory sample will not establish population prevalence or guarantee saturation. Actual recruitment numbers have not yet been entered.
目标是 6 位正式参与者，不代表已经招满。按照来港时间、路线熟悉度、导航经验和语言筛选。统一 Google Maps，但记录经验差异；6 个案例用于探索与比较，不做总体统计推断。
Sources and material notes  •  not part of the spoken script

Submitted Safari proposal (19 September 2026); Eric's confirmed six-person target and Google Maps condition; Word v2 Slide 5. Open Doodles sleek.svg is a generic illustration, not a participant portrait.

P2 Slide 06 Field site and route selection

texts.text: Select and rehearse a safe public route
Check duration, public access and safe crossings.
Include relevant level changes, bridge / subway connections and signage where feasible.
Check recording conditions; record device, language and voice settings.

SCRIPT 06  •  English and Chinese preparation notes

The walk will start at PolyU, but the destination and formal route are still undecided. We plan to scout safe crossings, public access, level changes, signage and recording conditions. We also need a feasible duration and a route unfamiliar to participants. We will give a destination rather than teach the path, and participants will use Google Maps without researcher turn-by-turn guidance. This photograph is urban context, not route or fieldwork evidence.
PolyU 起点已定，终点和路线仍待定。先踏勘安全、空间转换、路牌及时间，再确认参与者不熟悉。正式任务只给目的地，不提前教路；照片只是城市情境，不能当作踏勘成果。
Sources and material notes  •  not part of the spoken script
Word v2 Slide 6; Eric's route constraints. Unsplash NvSKcs-SiSc: urban context only. Actual destination, route map and scouting evidence remain TBC.

P2 Slide 08 Pilot and participant familiarisation

texts.text: Before main cases: test route, timing, recording and GPS export if permitted.
Two researchers independently code the same material; clarify ambiguous rules.
Record protocol changes. Keep pilot data separate from the six main cases.
Before each main walk: use the same briefing and a short unrelated route.
Check Google Maps setup, optional comments and the right to pause or stop.
Do not teach the main path. Exclude practice from main analysis.

texts.parentName: P2 Slide 08 Pilot and participant familiarisation
texts.text: A common procedure does not equalise ability; prior navigation experience remains different
SCRIPT 08  •  English and Chinese preparation notes

We distinguish the independent pilot from each participant's warm-up. The pilot tests our procedure, including timing, recording and the codebook, and remains separate from the six main cases. The warm-up uses a short, unrelated route and a shared briefing about app setup, optional comments and the right to pause or stop. We will not rehearse the main route. Practice is excluded from main analysis. Warm-up clarifies procedure; it does not equalise cognitive ability or previous experience.
Pilot 测试研究流程；warm-up 帮每位参与者理解任务。练习走另一条路，不教正式路线，也不计入正式分析。熟悉流程不等于统一认知能力。
Sources and material notes  •  not part of the spoken script
Word v2 Slide 8; HCI Research Methods Ch.7 pp.172–177 and Ch.8 p.210; Ways of Knowing in HCI practice-trial example pp.339–340. Open Doodles groovy.svg: generic illustration.
Start at the halt; end when walking resumes.
A GPS-only pause does not establish STOP.
PHONE_VIEW and SIGN_VIEW require discernible viewing.
Log event time, source and uncertainty. Record researcher prompts separately.
Near an exit: stopped and viewed phone
Record the visible actions and context. Keep the reason unknown until supported by a participant account.
No participant data or finding is represented here.
Preserve originals; optional GPS supports route context, not a psychological state
SCRIPT 09  •  English and Chinese preparation notes

The shared codebook defines observable actions such as stopping, phone viewing, phone input and sign viewing. We will record event times, environmental context and source references, while keeping unknown purposes unknown. A stop may simply be waiting for a signal. For each clip, we will retain a time anchor and distinguish full-journey coverage from partial footage. If GPS is approved and used, we will align timestamps to the same start marker and document gaps or drift. The table is an empty recording template, not collected data. Original notes and footage remain the analytical sources.
Codebook 是统一行为记录规则。记录停下、看手机、看路牌等，并标时间、环境和来源；不能把停下直接解释成困难。视频与可选 GPS 要对时，缺失或定位漂移要注明。表格是待填写模板，不是数据。
Sources and material notes  •  not part of the spoken script

Word v2 Appendices B–D. Wolff et al. (2024); Felner & Henderson (2022), doi:10.5888/pcd19.220134; GPS.gov accuracy guidance. STOP and PHONE_VIEW can co-occur; GPS alone does not establish either code.

texts.parentName: P2 Slide 10 Interviews and episode review
P2 Slide 10 Interviews and episode review

texts.text: What were you trying to work out?
Review 3–5 episodes, including a smooth / helpful moment.
Use neutral cues; allow uncertainty or no-effect answers.
Separate live words, recall and researcher interpretation.

texts.parentName: P2 Slide 10 Interviews and episode review
texts.text: Keep quotations distinct from summaries; retain the clip or note locator
SCRIPT 10  •  English and Chinese preparation notes

After the walk, we will first ask for an open account. Then we plan to review three to five focal episodes, including a smooth or helpful moment. We will ask what the participant was trying to work out, how the moment felt, and what helped or hindered. Neutral cues allow uncertainty and alternative explanations. Words spoken during the walk, retrospective explanations and our interpretations remain distinct. A quotation needs a reliable recording; otherwise we mark a paraphrase.
先让参与者整体回顾，再看 3–5 个片段，包括顺利的片段。用中性问题问当时想确认什么、感受如何、什么有帮助。现场原话、事后回忆和研究者解释分开；没有可靠录音就不要写成逐字引语。
Sources and material notes  •  not part of the spoken script
Word v2 Slide 10; Research Methods in HCI Ch.8 selected pp.198–201,206–213,219–223; Russell & Chi, Looking Back, selected pp.373–379.

texts.parentName: P2 Slide 11 Analysis and information classification
texts.text: One journey is one case; multiple episodes are not additional participants
SCRIPT 11  •  English and Chinese preparation notes

Each complete main walk is one case, with several episodes. We will review whole journeys, align sources, code actions, and add participant explanations to an episode matrix. We will compare helpful, difficult and ambiguous episodes within and across cases. Classification should connect information content and use with experienced interaction demands. Each design proposition needs supporting evidence and a boundary or counterexample. Multiple episodes from one person are not independent participants. Effectiveness requires later evaluation.
每个人的一次完整步行是一个案例，里面可以有多个片段。把记录、参与者解释和研究者判断对齐，再比较不同案例。分类与建议要有证据、反例或边界；一个人的多个片段不能当作多个人。
Sources and material notes  •  not part of the spoken script
Word v2 Appendix E; Research Methods in HCI Ch.7; Mohammed et al. (2023), doi:10.1177/16094069231197332. No empirical taxonomy or design effectiveness is claimed.
Widen permitted channels; retain eligibility. Narrow claims if fewer cases are available.
Pause or reschedule; use a documented, rehearsed backup if appropriate.
Route / weather changes and safety interventions

texts.text: GPS / recording fails or is declined

texts.parentName: GPS / recording fails or is declined
texts.text: Keep the approved observation / interview pathway. Respect pause, stop and withdrawal requests.

texts.parentName: GPS / recording fails or is declined
texts.text: Missing sources, capture limits and technical assistance
Fallback tools and any GPS addition must fit the approved protocol; logger remains TBC
SCRIPT 12  •  English and Chinese preparation notes

We have planned responses to recruitment, route and equipment problems. If recruitment falls short, we can widen permitted invitation channels while retaining eligibility, and narrow our claims if needed. Unsafe weather or an unsuitable route calls for rescheduling or a documented, rehearsed backup. If GPS fails or a participant declines it, we will retain the approved observation and interview pathway and mark that source as missing. Any recording fallback must also respect the approved protocol and consent. We will document these changes, rather than silently combine sessions conducted under different conditions.
招募不足时扩大合规渠道，不偷偷放宽条件；环境不安全就改期或用已踏勘的备选。GPS 拒绝／故障时保留获批的观察和访谈，注明缺失。所有变更要记录，不能把不同条件当作完全一样。
Sources and material notes  •  not part of the spoken script
Teacher P2 guideline: recruitment contingency; Word v2 Slide 12 and Appendices C–D. All fallbacks remain subject to approved ethics scope and participant choice.

Our group has confirmed the six-person target, Google Maps condition and PolyU starting point, and reports that ethics approval has been received. Route, GPS tool and actual recruitment and session counts need verified records. Add a dated scouting item or permitted de-identified pilot record before presenting. 已确认的是研究条件和伦理已收到，不是已完成人数。路线、工具、招募及完成数按真实记录填写。材料位置要换成有日期的踏勘或合规 pilot 记录；没有参与者数据就如实说明，只展示真实准备工作。

P2 Expanded 03 Knowledge gap and Literature review

texts.text: In unfamiliar walking navigation, which information episodes and interactions add attention and interaction burden, which effectively support orientation, action and confirmation, and how do these differences vary with context?

texts.parentName: P2 Expanded 03 Knowledge gap and Literature review
texts.text: Literature review: Navigation supports arrival, but can still make it supportive or burdensome.
Digital navigation changes wayfinding strategies and does not necessarily reduce anxiety.
Concurrent tasks can interfere when they draw on shared processing resources.
Urban mobile tasks fragment attention into brief interaction periods.
Map information involves a trade-off between spatial learning and cognitive load in VR.
When pedestrians request instructions varies with environmental and personal factors.
Tactile guidance can support eyes-free navigation in everyday use.
Phone glances correlate with stops and errors; the order of events remains unclear.
Wayfinding information can help users judge whether a walk is manageable.

Our knowledge gap is: in unfamiliar walking navigation, which information episodes and interactions add attention and interaction burden, which effectively support orientation, action and confirmation, and how do these differences vary with context?

The eight studies provide complementary evidence. Vaez shows that digital navigation changes strategies without necessarily reducing anxiety. Wickens explains competition for shared processing resources, and Oulasvirta shows fragmented attention in urban mobile tasks. Cheng examines the trade-off between map information, spatial learning and cognitive load in VR. Golab studies when pedestrians request instructions, while Pielot examines tactile navigation in everyday use. Shimokihara reports associations between phone glances, stops and errors but leaves their temporal order unresolved. Hardwicke shows how wayfinding information helps users judge manageable walks.

Together, these findings motivate studying specific information interactions in context. We will connect actions and participant explanations to distinguish experienced burden from useful guidance, confirmation and reassurance. Our methods do not directly measure the amount of attention consumed or cognitive load. The next slide illustrates why successful arrival can still involve an effortful experience.

我们的知识缺口是：在陌生环境的步行导航中，哪些信息片段与交互方式增加了使用者的注意力和交互负担，哪些有效支持了定向、行动与确认，以及这种差异如何随具体情境而变化。

八篇文献提供了互补的依据。Vaez 表明数字导航会改变寻路策略，却不一定降低焦虑；Wickens 解释共享处理资源的竞争；Oulasvirta 展示城市移动任务中注意力的碎片化。Cheng 研究虚拟导航中地图信息、空间学习与认知负荷的权衡；Golab 研究行人何时请求指令；Pielot 考察日常触觉导航。Shimokihara 发现看手机与停步、错误相关，但事件先后仍不明确；Hardwicke 展示导向信息如何帮助使用者判断步行是否适合自己。

这些证据共同支持我们研究具体情境中的信息交互，结合行动与参与者解释，区分被体验为负担的过程和有用的指引、确认与安心。我们的方法不直接测量注意力消耗量或认知负荷。下一页将用案例说明为什么成功抵达仍可能伴随费力的体验。

Evidence scope: Wickens (2008), multiple-resource theory; Oulasvirta et al. (2005), mobile Web-search tasks rather than navigation; Cheng et al. (2023), VR and 3/5/7-landmark EEG conditions; Golab et al. (2022), outdoor requests for spoken landmark instructions; Pielot et al. (2012), in-situ tactile-navigation logs; Vaez et al. (2020), unfamiliar-city navigation-aid groups; Hardwicke et al. (2024), park wayfinding interviews; Shimokihara et al. (2025), real-world smartphone-glance associations with unresolved temporal sequence. The table gives concise paraphrases of what the eight selected studies tell us, not their complete findings or declared research gaps. No claim that prior work ignores context or that redundancy invariably causes burden. The Repulse Bay journey and first-person expressions are fictional, not participant quotations. Full-trip fatigue is motivation; the study does not establish its cause.

Example:
A newcomer to Repulse Bay for holiday.

texts.parentName: P2 Expanded 04 Repulse Bay: an illustrative user journey
P2 Expanded 04 Repulse Bay: an illustrative user journey

texts.text:
Clear, timely cues
keep the journey manageable.
Destination reached ≠ an effortless navigation experience.
Identify which information and interactions support the journey, and which consume attention and effort.

Imagine a newcomer planning a relaxing day at Repulse Bay. They first find the right exit, follow street turns, resolve unclear cues and confirm the beach entrance.

The chart illustrates two possible experiences, not collected data. Clear, timely cues may keep the journey manageable. In the more demanding scenario, the traveller repeatedly switches between the map, signs and streets to work out what to do. They still reach the beach, but feel too drained to enjoy it.

Both scenarios reach the destination. The difference is the effort experienced along the way. This motivates our question: which information episodes and interactions support navigation, and which add attention or interaction burden? Our actual study examines a short unfamiliar walk, rather than testing a whole Repulse Bay trip or measuring energy depletion.

想象一位初到香港的人，计划去浅水湾度过轻松的一天。途中，他需要寻找正确出口、沿街转弯、解决不清楚的线索，最后确认海滩入口。

图中展示两种可能的体验，不是已收集的数据。清楚、及时的线索可能让旅程较容易应对。另一种情境中，他需要不断在地图、路牌和街道之间切换、反复核对，才能判断下一步。最终虽然抵达海滩，却觉得已经没有多少精力继续游玩。

两种情境都完成了抵达，区别在于过程中的费力程度。这说明我们为什么要研究哪些信息片段和交互方式提供支持，哪些增加注意力或交互负担。正式研究聚焦一段陌生短途步行，并不直接测试整段浅水湾出行或测量精力耗竭。

Illustrative user journey adapted structurally from the user's reference: phase bands, stage cards, a qualitative experience curve, an arrival highlight and a takeaway. All stages, curves, relative heights and first-person expressions are fictional. The vertical dimension is perceived energy available for exploring, without a scale, thresholds or measurements. The two lines are contrasting hypothetical experiences, not compared prototypes or study conditions. The story motivates the study; it does not establish navigation as the cause of fatigue. Heat, physical exertion, mood, time pressure and prior tiredness remain possible explanations. Formal fieldwork is a short unfamiliar walking task. Research support is synthesised on the preceding literature page.

texts.parentName: P2 Expanded 05 Paradigm, lens and method rationale

texts.text: Pragmatism guides our method choices because we want evidence that can inform design decisions in this context. Multiple Resource Theory is a sensitising lens for considering competing demands. We will use a focused qualitative study, with one complete walk as one case. Observation and later interviews let us examine actions and participants' explanations together.
实用主义指导我们选择方法，因为我们希望获得能够为这一情境下的设计决定提供依据的证据。多重资源理论作为启发性视角，帮助我们考虑不同任务要求之间的竞争。我们采用聚焦的定性研究，以一次完整步行为一个案例。观察和后续访谈让我们能够结合行动与参与者的解释进行研究。

Each method helps us understand a different part of the same journey. Observation records the actions and their surroundings. Semi-structured interviews explore what participants were trying to do and how the experience felt. Reviewing selected episodes connects those explanations to specific moments. We then analyse each walk and compare cases to develop contextual information categories and preliminary design guidance.
每种方法帮助我们理解同一次步行的不同方面。现场观察记录行动顺序和周围情境；半结构式访谈了解参与者当时想做什么，以及他们的体验。回顾选定片段，把这些解释与具体时刻联系起来。最后，我们先分析每次完整步行，再比较不同案例，形成情境化的信息分类和初步设计建议。

We have four research objectives. First, we will identify information needs and observable interaction episodes across an unfamiliar walking journey. Second, we will identify participant-reported moments of feeling overwhelmed, examine possible sources of difficulty, and explore perceived consequences for enjoyment, confidence, continued exploration and reaching the destination. Third, we will develop a classification linking information roles, contextual demands and participant explanations, including contrasting cases. Finally, we will derive evidence-linked guidance for presenting timing, detail and delivery, with clear limits on what has been evaluated.

我们有四项研究目标。第一，识别陌生环境步行旅程中的信息需求，以及可观察的交互片段。第二，识别参与者报告的感到不知所措的时刻，探究可能的困难来源，以及他们认为这些经历对游玩享受、信心、继续探索和抵达目的地产生了什么影响。第三，形成一个分类，将信息的作用、情境要求与参与者的解释联系起来，并纳入相互对照的案例。第四，基于证据提出有关信息呈现时机、细节程度和传递方式的设计建议，并明确哪些内容已经被研究、哪些仍未经过评估。

texts.parentName: Feasible scope, with room for depth

texts.text: Feasible scope, with room for depth

Six cases fit the project schedule and allow detailed observation,
interviewing, within-case analysis and cross-case comparison.

If six cases provide insufficient evidence, recruitment will continue until interpretations are
adequately supported or additional cases yield little substantive new insight.

We acknowledge the limits of this study. Given the project timeline, this is a focused, exploratory study in which each case combines a walking observation with an in-depth interview. We propose six participants as an initial target for three reasons. First, we will screen participants against our study criteria, so each case is relevant to the research question. Screening supports relevance; it does not guarantee rich data. Second, six cases are feasible within the schedule while allowing us to examine each journey and interview in depth, then compare cases. Third, we will review the evidence iteratively. If key questions remain unresolved, we will recruit further participants to address those gaps. We will assess whether interpretations are well supported and whether additional cases bring substantively new insights, rather than assume that six guarantees saturation. If time prevents further recruitment, we will narrow our claims and report the remaining limitations.

我们首先承认研究的有限性。考虑到项目时间，这是一个范围有限的探索性研究，每个案例都包含步行观察和深入访谈。我们将六位参与者作为初始目标，理由有三点。第一，我们会依据研究标准筛选参与者，确保案例与研究问题相关；筛选有助于提高相关性，但不能保证资料一定丰富。第二，六个案例在项目时间上可行，也给我们机会深入整理每次步行与访谈，先做案例内分析，再做跨案例比较。第三，我们会边收集边检查证据。如果关键问题仍未得到充分解释，就继续招募，针对证据缺口补充案例；并检查解释是否得到充分支持，以及新增案例是否仍带来实质性的新认识。我们不会预先断言六人一定达到饱和。如果时间限制使我们无法继续招募，就收窄结论，并明确报告尚未解决的不足。

Sample size and recruitment strategy are study-design decisions. Participant screening establishes relevance rather than guaranteeing data quality. Assess diminishing new insight alongside evidence quality and unresolved differences; do not treat six as a universal saturation threshold.

正式步行前，我们需要让每个人都理解研究流程。独立预试会检查路线、时间和记录规则。随后，每位参与者接受同样的说明，并完成一段短的教学步行。我们解释谁负责观察、会记录什么，以及如何暂停或退出。参与者练习使用 Google Maps，并用自己的话复述任务。这有助于减少流程上的不确定，但能力差异和观察效应仍可能存在。练习记录单独保存。下一页展示我们拟议的热身路线。

texts.text: The purpose of this session is to establish a shared understanding of the research procedure before the main walk. Participants should understand the task, who will observe them, what will be recorded, and how they can pause or withdraw. A short practice lets them experience the observation and recording setup and ask procedural questions in advance. We use the same briefing and teach-back check for everyone, aiming to reduce differences caused by unclear instructions or unfamiliar research procedures. This standardises procedural understanding; it does not equalise navigation skills or eliminate observer effects. The campus route shown here is a proposed practice setting, rather than the purpose of the session. Its distance, access and Google Maps routing still need checking. We will not preview the formal route or coach navigation behaviour. Practice records and additional clarifications are logged separately, and the timer is reset before the main task.

这个环节的核心目的，是在正式步行前，让所有参与者对研究任务和流程形成一致、清楚的理解。大家需要知道自己要做什么、谁会观察、记录哪些资料，以及如何暂停或退出。短距离练习让参与者提前体验被观察和记录的过程，并有机会提出流程上的疑问。我们对每个人采用相同的说明和复述检查，尽量减少因指令不清楚、不了解流程或不熟悉记录安排而引入的额外差异。这里统一的是对研究流程的理解，不代表所有人的导航能力相同，也不意味着能够完全消除观察效应。图中的校园路线只是实施练习的候选场景，实际距离、通行情况及 Google Maps 路线仍需确认。练习不提前透露正式路线，也不指导参与者应该怎样导航。练习资料和额外说明单独记录，正式任务开始前重新计时。

After the tutorial, we return to the South Gate meeting point to get ready for the main walk. We plan to have two researchers: one watches the participant's actions and looks out for safety; the other records events and their timing.

Before the walk starts, we check consent, phone settings and clock synchronisation. We call the start time T0. Any questions or device adjustments wait until we reach a safe place to stop. For the interview, we'll have one moderator, with a notetaker if needed.

Our main record will be fieldnotes taken during the walk, with a time marked for each event. We'll note what the participant does, what's happening around them, and any prompts from us. We'll then expand these notes soon after the session.

With consent, short video clips can help us check details and help participants recall specific moments. GPS adds another piece: where they walked and when. Let me show you how we plan to record that.
带时间戳的现场笔记仍是主要记录。我们在事件发生时记下行动、周围条件和研究员提示，并及时扩写简短笔记。经同意拍摄的短片可支持之后的核对和回顾。下一页说明手机 GPS 的记录流程，它补充路线和时间背景，仍需要预试验证。

Participants will navigate with Google Maps on their own phones. A separate app will record the route in the background: Open GPX Tracker on iPhone, or BasicAirData GPS Logger on Android. We still need to test this setup in the pilot.

We start the recorder, open Google Maps, and mark T0 when the main walk begins. Recording continues through normal stops. At the destination, we mark the end time and export a GPX file. We check timestamps and gaps, then match the track with our fieldnotes. Pace is extra information, not a target. This screenshot shows Open GPX Tracker before recording, not a participant's route.

除了现场笔记，我们计划用每位参与者自己的手机记录带时间戳的轨迹。iPhone 使用 Open GPX Tracker，Android 使用 BasicAirData GPS Logger，两者都需要经过预试验证。我们先启动记录器，再回到 Google Maps，并标记正式 T0。普通停步时继续记录。到终点后标记结束时间，保存并导出一个 GPX 文件。先检查时间戳和缺失段，再与事件表对齐。配速只作辅助。这张截图展示的是开始记录前的界面，不是参与者数据。

Software instructions: Merlos (n.d.), Open GPX Tracker developer README and ViewController documentation; BasicAirData (n.d.), GPS Logger getting-started guide. iPhone: Pause, Save/name, Share GPX through the system share sheet (e.g. Files). Android: enable Export Tracks in GPX in Settings; Stop, Tracklist, select track, Export/Share. Actual menu wording and background recording with Google Maps require pilot checks on each phone. Formal T0/end anchors in fieldnotes define the main interval, excluding logger setup, tutorial and transfer. Keep original UTC timestamps, derive HKT and elapsed T0 for matching. Preserve the raw GPX, mark gaps/jumps and do not delete the phone copy until export is verified. Collect only consented task-window data in approved storage. Pace = elapsed formal-task minutes / acceptable distance in km; supplementary only, no target or causal inference. Group operational definitions. Coding principles: Wolff et al. (2024); Felner & Henderson (2022). Pilot calibration remains TBC.

New codes may be added as behaviours emerge in interviews, e.g. PHONE_SEARCH
for searching for navigation-related information on a phone.

The GPS track helps us locate an event. Our codebook helps us describe what happened. We start with seven action labels, and more than one can apply to the same event.

For example, holding a phone isn't enough to count as PHONE_VIEW: we need to see the person looking at it. A head turn doesn't necessarily mean they're reading a sign. For HELP_REQUEST, we need to hear or reliably note a request for help. If we can't tell what happened, we mark it as uncertain.

The codebook can expand when interviews reveal behaviours not captured by the initial labels. For example, if a participant reports searching for navigation-related information on their phone, we may add PHONE_SEARCH. We will define its inclusion and exclusion criteria, document the update and review earlier cases consistently. Interview-reported behaviour will remain distinguishable from directly observed evidence.

轨迹帮助我们定位片段；为了描述发生了什么，编码手册先使用七种可见行动标签，并允许重叠。拿着手机不能证明正在看地图，转头也不能证明正在读标识。HELP_REQUEST 需要听到或可靠记下求助请求。每个编码都记录依据，模糊事件仍保留为不确定。

编码手册也可以随着访谈中发现的新行为而扩充。例如，参与者说明自己曾在导航途中用手机查询相关信息，我们可以新增 PHONE_SEARCH。新增编码需要明确纳入与排除标准、记录修订，并一致地回查先前案例。同时，访谈中自述的行为与直接观察到的行为仍要区分，不能把自述自动当作现场观察证据。

This is the worksheet we'll use to record those events. Each row links a participant and an event to its timing, action codes, surroundings and a description of what we actually observed.

After the walk, we add what the participant told us and our own interpretation in separate fields. We also note whether their account is an exact quote, a paraphrase, or unavailable. Source references, uncertainty notes, the coder's name and the codebook version help us trace each entry back to its evidence.
这些事件会填入这张记录表。每行包括案例和事件编号、相对于 T0 的时间、编码、情境及原始描述。参与者陈述和研究员解释分别记录。来源编号、可信程度、编码者和版本使记录可以追溯。在比较案例之前，我们会区分已核实的原话、转述和未知陈述。

Here's a made-up example of how those pieces fit together. A participant stops near a crossing and then looks at their phone. That's what we observe and record.

Later, we ask what they were trying to do. Their answer may help us understand the event, but we keep it separate from our interpretation. Were they checking the route, waiting for traffic, or doing something else? We consider these possibilities before drawing a conclusion. This slide shows our reasoning process; it doesn't contain participant data.
这个例子是假设性的。假设记录表在路口附近记下先停步、后查看手机的行为。后续陈述可能解释参与者当时想做什么。我们会把这个解释单独保留，再同时考虑导航不确定和等候交通等其他解释。这张表用于示范推理过程，不含参与者数据。

The camera provides an auxiliary record for researchers to check the accuracy of the primary fieldnotes. Researchers can revisit relevant segments to verify observable event details and timing, and document any corrections or unresolved discrepancies. The footage will not be coded or analysed as a separate dataset; the primary notes remain the main record.

The observer could wear an action camera on a chest mount, such as the GoPro Chesty shown here. The equipment has not yet been selected. Before use, we need to test comfort, framing and recording controls, and check consent, bystander privacy and site restrictions. Eric has reported receiving ethics approval; its scope for camera and GPS recording still needs confirmation. Next, we will explain the post-walk interview.

相机用于提供辅助记录，帮助研究人员核对主要现场笔记的准确性。研究人员可以回看相关片段，检查可见事件的细节和时间，并记录必要的更正或仍未解决的差异。录像不会作为独立资料集进行编码或分析，primary notes 仍然是主要记录。

texts.parentName: P2 Expanded 27 Shared semi-structured interview guide
P2 Expanded 27 Shared semi-structured interview guide

texts.text: How would you describe the walk?
What information did you look for? Which sources did you use?
What helped you decide where to go next?
Which moments were straightforward? Was anything unclear?
When or how would you prefer to receive that information?

texts.parentName: P2 Expanded 27 Shared semi-structured interview guide
texts.text: Same core topics for all six. Order and follow-up can vary. Ask one question at a time, allow pauses and follow the participant’s own wording.

texts.parentName: P2 Expanded 27 Shared semi-structured interview guide
texts.text: Lazar et al. (2017), pp. 198–200, 207–208. These prompts are group drafts, not book quotations.

After the walk, we'll use a semi-structured interview to understand the participant's experience.

We'll cover the same core topics with everyone: what information they looked for, how they decided where to go next, and which moments felt clear or confusing.

We'll begin with, "How would you describe the walk?" Then we'll follow up on their answers, one question at a time. The topics stay consistent, but the order and follow-up questions can vary.

步行结束后，我们会通过半结构式访谈了解参与者的体验。

每个人都会围绕相同的核心话题展开：他们寻找了什么信息、如何决定下一步往哪里走，以及哪些时刻清楚或令人困惑。

我们先问「你会怎样描述这次步行？」再根据回答追问，每次只问一个问题。核心话题保持一致，但提问顺序和后续追问可以不同。
Lazar et al. (2017), pp. 198–200, 207–208. These prompts are group drafts, not book quotations.
3–5 logged episodes, including smooth or helpful moments.
Show a consented short clip or still. Use notes if no recording exists.

Do you remember this moment?
What was happening here?
What were you trying to do?

Accept “I don’t remember” and “it had no effect.” 
Ask “Was anything unclear, or was this straightforward?” 
Avoid assuming overload or difficulty. 
Log cue source and any mismatch with live notes.
Russell & Chi (2014), pp. 373–379; Lazar et al. (2017), pp. 207–208. Recall can be reconstructive.

We'll then look back at three to five moments from our observation notes, including moments when navigation went smoothly.

With consent, a short clip or still image can help the participant recall what happened. If we don't have a recording, we'll use our notes.

We might ask, "Do you remember this moment?" and then, "What were you trying to do?" It's fine if they don't remember. We won't assume that stopping or checking the phone means difficulty, and we'll record any differences between their account and our notes.

然后，我们会回顾现场观察笔记中的三至五个时刻，也包括导航顺利的时刻。

在获得同意的情况下，短片或静态图可以帮助参与者回忆；没有影像时，就使用现场笔记。

我们可以先问「你记得这个时刻吗？」再问「你当时想做什么？」不记得也没关系。我们不会把停步或看手机直接当成困难，也会记录他们的描述与笔记之间的差异。
Russell & Chi (2014), pp. 373–379; Lazar et al. (2017), pp. 207–208. Recall can be reconstructive.

texts.parentName: P2 Expanded 29 Analysis and information classification

Patterns and differences within and across cases
Information roles, contexts and associated interaction burdens

texts.parentName: P2 Expanded 29 Analysis and information classification
texts.text: Analysis dimensions: Information content, source, purpose, context, significance and associated interaction burden. Classification will consider both helpful interactions and difficulties, while design implications require further validation.

texts.parentName: P2 Expanded 29 Analysis and information classification
texts.text: Lazar et al. (2017), pp. 176–177; Wickens (2008). Classification dimensions are provisional group choices.

Together, these records will help us understand each person's walk.

For each episode, we'll look at the information involved, how it was used, and whether the participant described it as helpful or difficult. We'll keep our observations separate from our interpretation.

Then we'll compare the six planned cases, looking for recurring patterns, differences and other possible explanations.

From this, we aim to develop a provisional classification of navigation information and suggest when and how it could be delivered. The design suggestions will still need further testing.

这些记录放在一起，会帮助我们理解每个人的完整步行经历。

针对每个片段，我们会看涉及哪些信息、信息如何被使用，以及参与者是否认为它有帮助或造成困难。直接观察到的事实会与研究者的解释分开记录。

接下来比较计划中的六个案例，寻找重复出现的模式、案例之间的差异，以及其他可能的解释。

我们希望据此形成暂定的导航信息分类，并提出信息传达时机与方式的建议。这些设计建议仍需要进一步验证。
Lazar et al. (2017), pp. 176–177; Wickens (2008). Classification dimensions are provisional group choices.
Record changes before main sessions. Changes outside approved scope require tutor clearance before use.
Widen recruitment within criteria. Replace familiar-route volunteers.
Eligibility, achieved N and justified changes.
Reschedule or use a previously checked backup.
Route change, weather, access and comparability.
Continue with consented live notes. Flag missing auxiliary coverage.
Missing segments, time offsets and source gaps.
Pause or stop. Follow consent and approved handling.
R_PROMPT, reason and usable / excluded evidence.
Lazar et al. (2017), pp. 175–176. Teacher P2 guideline specifically requests participant-recruitment contingencies.

We also have backup plans for problems during data collection.

If recruitment falls short, we'll widen it within our existing criteria. Changes outside the approved scope will need tutor clearance.

If weather or access makes a route unsafe, we'll reschedule or use a previously checked backup.

If the camera or GPS fails, we'll still have our live observation notes as the primary record. We'll document missing recordings and any safety intervention, because these may affect how we interpret the walk.

texts.text: Working gap: connect information needs, observable episodes and newcomers’ accounts on an unfamiliar Hong Kong walk. This remains a proposition to test against literature and field evidence.

Our selected literature discusses workload, instruction timing, tactile guidance and smartphone glances. It gives us reasons to examine navigation as a sequence of situated decisions. Our working gap connects information needs, visible actions and newcomers' reported help or difficulty. The selected reading does not establish the full state of Hong Kong navigation research.
